stories.research_notes:
Here’s what sources show about the event “Volunteers pack Thanksgiving groceries for 2,000 families” attributed to New Birth Church in Stonecrest, Georgia:

---

### What Happened

- New Birth Missionary Baptist Church, in partnership with DeKalb County and several community organizations (including V-103 and 1-800TruckWreck) held a **drive-through giveaway** of free turkeys, fresh produce, and groceries for Metro Atlanta families on **Thursday, November 19, 2026**. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))

- The event aimed to serve **2,000 families**, and was scheduled from **6:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m.** or until supplies were exhausted. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))

- DeKalb County contributed **2,000 boxes of fresh produce**. Produce providers also included a local farm called aGROWKulture Urban Farm, supplying collard greens, cabbage, sweet corn, zucchini, and yellow squash. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))

- Families did **not** need to apply, register, or show proof of income. Food was distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))

- Hundreds of volunteers participated in organizing, loading groceries into trunks, and directing traffic. Long vehicle lines were reported starting as early as 4 p.m. the night before. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))

---

### What Is Measured vs. What Is a Plan

- **Completed / Measured Outcomes**  
  • The event took place on Nov. 19, 2026. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))  
  • It had the goal to serve 2,000 families. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))  
  • DeKalb County provided 2,000 boxes of fresh produce. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))  

- **Plans or Aims**  
  • “Aimed to serve 2,000 families” is an announced goal; the sources do *not* contain explicit confirmation that all 2,000 families were ultimately served (i.e. whether the supply lasted exactly until that goal was reached). ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))

---

### Independent Verification & Source Types

- **Original/Primary Source**: CBS News Atlanta article “Metro Atlanta families line up hours early for free Thanksgiving turkeys, groceries in Stonecrest” provides on-site reporting by CBS. ([cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/metro-atlanta-families-line-up-hours-early-for-free-thanksgiving-turkeys-groceries-in-stonecrest/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Independent Source**: WSB-TV (Atlanta) covers the same event — giving overlapping details (2,000 families, free turkeys & produce, timing, venue) in local news reporting. ([wsbtv.com](https://www.wsbtv.com/news/local/2000-families-receive-free-turkeys-fresh-produce-ahead-thanksgiving/PNNOOFZTOZCH5NHYO6B7RYY3RE/?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Conclusion

This event was not just an announcement or pledge — it actually took place on November 19, 2026. The volunteers did distribute free turkeys, groceries, and fresh produce in a drive-through format to support up to 2,000 families, with no income verification required. However, the reports do *not* conclusively confirm whether **all** 2,000 families were served (e.g., whether supplies ran short before the target was met).

stories.research_notes:
Here’s a research note on what has *actually* happened to date with the Swinomish Tribe’s clam garden revival, based on live sources. This clarifies what’s completed versus what’s in progress.

---

## What is the project

- The Swinomish Indian Tribal Community (SITC) is reviving an ancient Indigenous mariculture practice of clam gardening. A clam garden is built by installing a rock wall in the intertidal zone; behind it, sediment and shell fragments accumulate, creating terraces favorable for clams and other species. ([waseagrant.uw.edu](https://waseagrant.uw.edu/2023/06/restoring-tradition-place-and-connection-through-a-clam-garden/?utm_source=openai))  
- Their goal includes boosting clam populations (notably littleneck and butter clams), restoring species diversity, enhancing food sovereignty, transmitting cultural knowledge between generations, and increasing ecological and socio-cultural resilience. ([nwcasc.uw.edu](https://nwcasc.uw.edu/science/project/clam-gardens-an-indigenous-community-driven-climate-adaptation-strategy-to-manage-aquatic-species-and-habitats-in-the-pacific-northwest/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Key dates & activities completed

- **September 2021**: Swinomish Canoe Family blessed the selected site. ([eopugetsound.org](https://www.eopugetsound.org/article/first-modern-clam-garden-takes-shape-puget-sound?utm_source=openai))  
- **August 2022**: Construction began—first rocks laid for the clam garden wall on Kiket Island, in the Kukutali Preserve. ([waseagrant.uw.edu](https://waseagrant.uw.edu/2023/06/restoring-tradition-place-and-connection-through-a-clam-garden/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Mid-2023**: Community involvement events, including moving tens of tons of rocks to build and extend the wall (e.g. “about 60 people” over two days, moving 35 tons of rocks) and holding wall building & beach tending events. ([waseagrant.uw.edu](https://waseagrant.uw.edu/2023/06/restoring-tradition-place-and-connection-through-a-clam-garden/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What is *still* in progress

- **Ecological outcomes** (clam abundance, growth, mortality etc.) are *not yet fully measured*—data collection is ongoing. A “Before-After-Impact-Control” (BAIC) study spans 2021–2025 to monitor ecological changes at the restored clam garden versus control beach sites. ([usgs.gov](https://www.usgs.gov/data/nearshore-substrate-macrophyte-invertebrate-and-clam-data-collected-field-sites-pre-and-post?utm_source=openai))  
- **Wall and terrace performance** over time is under observation—how well the structure retains sediment, supports clams, responds to waves, heat, ocean acidification, etc. ([nwcasc.uw.edu](https://nwcasc.uw.edu/science/project/how-do-long-wave-dynamics-and-temperature-variability-affect-clam-gardens-in-the-northwest/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Harvesting for food**: While the shellfish there are intended for future subsistence harvest, no reports yet confirm harvesting has begun for human consumption. The site was chosen to be “free from toxins” and usable for subsistence rather than commercial purposes. ([uri.edu](https://www.uri.edu/magazine/wp-content/uploads/magazine/sites/13/2026/04/Final_Spring-2026_Online.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Measured outcomes vs pledges/plans

| Status | Completed / Measured | Pledge / Plan / Underway |
|---|---|---|
| Wall construction & site establishment | ✔ Wall built (starting August 2022), wall ~61 meters long so far. ([swinomish-nsn.gov](https://www.swinomish-nsn.gov/sites/g/files/vyhlif8876/files/media/fisheries/file/4541/pathwaysdocumentfeb2025_print.pdf?utm_source=openai)) | Expansion and tending continue; final shape still evolving. ([swinomish-nsn.gov](https://www.swinomish-nsn.gov/sites/g/files/vyhlif8876/files/media/fisheries/file/4541/pathwaysdocumentfeb2025_print.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| Community and cultural engagement | ✔ Multiple events since 2022 – beach tending, traditional knowledge transmission, multiple communities involved. ([swinomish-nsn.gov](https://www.swinomish-nsn.gov/sites/g/files/vyhlif8876/files/media/fisheries/file/4541/pathwaysdocumentfeb2025_print.pdf?utm_source=openai)) | Continued engagement planned: more events, sharing lessons, supporting other tribes. ([swinomish-nsn.gov](https://www.swinomish-nsn.gov/sites/g/files/vyhlif8876/files/media/fisheries/file/4541/pathwaysdocumentfeb2025_print.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| Ecological benefits (clam / species metrics) | ❓ Not yet conclusively measured—baseline and early monitoring are underway. ([usgs.gov](https://www.usgs.gov/data/nearshore-substrate-macrophyte-invertebrate-and-clam-data-collected-field-sites-pre-and-post?utm_source=openai)) | Study plans extend over years; hypotheses are that clam abundance, size, survival, and diversity will increase. ([nwcasc.uw.edu](https://nwcasc.uw.edu/science/project/how-do-long-wave-dynamics-and-temperature-variability-affect-clam-gardens-in-the-northwest/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Food harvest for human consumption | ❗ No evidence yet of regular harvesting for food—site chosen with that goal in mind but not yet realized. ([uri.edu](https://www.uri.edu/magazine/wp-content/uploads/magazine/sites/13/2026/04/Final_Spring-2026_Online.pdf?utm_source=openai)) | Intended future subsistence harvests are part of project aims. ([nwcasc.uw.edu](https://nwcasc.uw.edu/science/project/clam-gardens-an-indigenous-community-driven-climate-adaptation-strategy-to-manage-aquatic-species-and-habitats-in-the-pacific-northwest/?utm_source=openai)) |

---

## Primary sources

- **Data release**: US Geological Survey (USGS) published “Nearshore substrate, macrophyte, invertebrate, and clam data collected at field sites pre- and post-installation … (2021-2025)” which shows the monitoring methods and early data. ([usgs.gov](https://www.usgs.gov/data/nearshore-substrate-macrophyte-invertebrate-and-clam-data-collected-field-sites-pre-and-post?utm_source=openai))  
- **Journal article**: “Reviving the past to protect the future: developing a social-ecological clam garden site-selection model” (2025) details how the site was chosen via combined ecological and social criteria, plus community surveys. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1080/1943815X.2025.2573346?utm_source=openai))  
- **Case studies document (Pathways)** by Swinomish Tribe Fisheries Department describes ecological, socio-cultural surveys, and outcomes so far. ([swinomish-nsn.gov](https://www.swinomish-nsn.gov/sites/g/files/vyhlif8876/files/media/fisheries/file/4541/pathwaysdocumentfeb2025_print.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Independent reporting & notes

- Oregon Field Guide (OPB/PBS) has aired a segment covering the clam garden’s work, noting restoration of ancestral access, site selection over 15 candidate beaches, community hope for increased shellfish population and diversity. ([pbs.org](https://www.pbs.org/video/rediscovering-ancient-clam-gardens-to-feed-the-future-mftu5d/?utm_source=openai))  
- Cascadia Daily News reports on community wall‐building, movement of rocks, and that the garden is *not yet finished* but making concrete progress. ([cascadiadaily.com](https://www.cascadiadaily.com/2023/jun/05/swinomish-community-creates-clam-garden-on-reclaimed-lands/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Summary: What *actually* has happened by Nov 2026

- The first modern clam garden in the U.S. has been built (beginning Aug 2022) by the Swinomish tribe on ancestral beach lands at Kiket Island / Kukutali Preserve.  
- A rock wall roughly 61 meters long has been installed; tens of tons of rocks have been placed; initial ecological and cultural engagement is underway.  
- Long-term ecological monitoring (2021–2025) has been established with control sites; socio-cultural benefits are being documented (community events, knowledge transfer, reconnection to place).  
- No evidence yet of regular human harvest for food; ecological outcomes (clam growth, abundance, improved species diversity) are not yet fully documented or published with definitive results.  

---

If you like, I can dig into the **latest available monitoring data** to see numeric outcomes so far (clam densities, size, mortality, etc.) and whether any human harvests have taken place yet. Do you want that?
